notes:
- Company: BlueQuarry Product AI — mid-market SaaS (product analytics/search).
- Started on Redwood hosted API for embeddings/search; impressed by token-level cost breakdown in Console.
- Use-case mix: embeddings for search ranking (primary), chat-based product assistant (secondary), occasional reranking for recommendations.
- Latency targets: p95 chat <= 200ms; embeddings throughput 150 req/s during business hours. Cost sensitivity: high (startup margins).
- Initial hosted POC: ~3M tokens/mo, uplifted to 6M during blackbox test. Observed step-change with caching.
- Decision path: product engineering (VP Product + Eng manager) -> infra/security -> procurement/legal.
- Why Dedicated: predictable throughput for peak analytics/reporting window, want private VPC and dedicated GPU pools to hit p95 SLA.
- Pricing asks from customer: 12–18 month commit, monthly ramp schedule, burst credits for seasonal spikes, clear overage formulas (prefer per-hour cap), 30% discount threshold for commit >200K tokens/day equivalent.
- Redwood proposals so far: commit tiers at 50k/150k/300k token-equivalents with burst pool (2x) and overage at 1.25x unit price; customer pushing for overage cap and ability to pre-buy burst credits.
- Legal: wants explicit data residency + IP carving; redline pending. Security: needs KMS integration details (customer-managed).
- SE notes: Marcus confirmed quantization profile tradeoffs — can hit latency SLO with int8 + KV cache for chat. POC showed 28% less per-token cost vs hosted baseline when using batching & cache.
- POC metrics attached in drive (see pricing sheet).
- Quote outstanding: final pricing sheet v3 uploaded. Procurement asked for a formal SOW and ramp milestones tied to invoice schedule.
- Customer quote: "We need firm predictability — if we commit, we expect predictable unit pricing and a transparent burst mechanism."
- Next steps: finalize commit level, draft SOW, schedule legal 1:1 (Evelyn to coordinate), deliver final SLA appendix.
- Risks: procurement windows (end of Q1 budget), security delays on KMS, potential competitor counter-offer (Anthropic on reserved endpoints).
- Internal ask: Pricing Ops to model 2 ramp scenarios (fast: 3 months to full commit, slow: 6 months) + provide overage cap options.
